text:
Maya: Quick heads up — I spun up plankton-embed-v1.2-int8 on staging and ran the noise-robustness k-fold pipeline (k=5) with synthetic token-drop and paraphrase noise. TL;DR: recall@10 ~ 0.805 vs baseline 0.841; recall@1 hit hardest on short queries. Need triage.

Jon: which baseline are you comparing to? prod heron or the last checked revision? also can you paste per-fold numbers?

Maya: baseline is heron-prod (heron-embed-v2). Per-fold CSV below:

```
fold,recall@1,recall@10
1,0.731,0.802
2,0.725,0.808
3,0.719,0.795
4,0.740,0.822
5,0.728,0.800
mean,0.729,0.805
prod-heron,0.794,0.841
```

Sasha: okay — numbers look consistent across folds (low variance). Did you apply any centering/whitening before computing similarity? clustering metrics?

Maya: I used our standard pipeline: L2-normalize after the projection. No whitening in this run. Clustering silhouette went from 0.62 (prod) -> 0.57 (plankton-int8). Also ran an orthogonality probe: avg abs dot mag increased 0.012 -> 0.019.

Jon: interesting. did you test per-channel vs per-tensor quant? often projection layers are sensitive.

Maya: yes — per-channel symmetric 8-bit was used for the main run. I also tried per-tensor; per-tensor was worse on recall@1 by ~2.4 points (mean).

Sasha: short queries often suffer because vector norms are small and quantization noise dominates. Can you run the short-query subset (len<8 tokens) separately?

Maya: ran that: baseline recall@1 on short subset = 0.68, plankton-int8 = 0.59 — big drop. recall@10 less affected (0.78 -> 0.74). Hypothesis: projection bias + quant scale clipping.

Jon: thanks. let's try two quick experiments: 1) per-channel INT8 but with clamp at 2.5 std dev for the proj weights, 2) mixed-precision for the final projection (keep fp16 for projection, int8 elsewhere). can you queue those?

Sasha: I'll open a small PR to toggle the clamp and add the per-channel scale override flag. Also we should consider an int4 per-channel run if runtime supports it (to check cost vs quality).

Maya: Proposed rollout/mitigation plan: 1) run clamp + mixed-precision experiments on staging overnight, 2) evaluate with our short-query holdout + silhouette + orthogonality probes, 3) if fails, add a fallback routing policy in Redwood: route queries with len<8 to heron-prod for now. Thoughts?

Jon: sounds good. for the A/B we should capture rerank click telemetry and session-level recency metrics. :thumbsup:

eval-bot: Job completed — full run artifacts: https://evals.internal/runs/3723456789-plankton-noise. Artifacts: embeddings.npy, per_fold.csv, silhouette.png, orthogonality.csv

Maya: thanks — grabbing artifacts now. tagging @Sasha to pick up the clamp PR. :eyes:

Sasha: on it, I'll post a short note with the PR link and the staging job IDs once queued.

Maya: closing loop — will post an updated summary tomorrow with per-experiment diffs and latency/cost delta for mixed-precision.

Jon: appreciated.
